title: Understanding DNS, domains, and IP addresses
content:
## What is DNS Really?

DNS is often called the phonebook of the internet, but that analogy obscures its distributed hierarchical nature.

When you type `arveix.cc` into your browser, your operating system has no idea which machine in the world to connect to until it queries a DNS recursive resolver.

> Without DNS caching at every layer (browser, OS, router, ISP), the global internet infrastructure would collapse under the volume of lookups.

### The Resolution Chain

1. **Root Nameservers (`.`):** There are 13 logical root server addresses managed by ICANN.
2. **TLD Nameservers (`.cc`):** Direct queries to the authoritative nameserver for that specific top-level domain.
3. **Authoritative Nameservers:** The definitive host holding the actual resource records (`A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `MX`, `TXT`).

```bash
# Inspect the full recursive trace using dig
dig +trace arveix.cc
```

---

## Common DNS Record Types

- `A Record`: Maps a domain to an IPv4 address (e.g. `192.0.2.1`).
- `AAAA Record`: Maps a domain to a 128-bit IPv6 address.
- `CNAME Record`: An alias that points one name to another hostname.
- `TXT Record`: Arbitrary text data, crucial for SPF, DKIM, and site verification.

title: TCP vs UDP: when does the difference matter?
content:
## The Fundamental Tradeoff

At Layer 4 of the OSI model, TCP and UDP present two fundamentally different engineering philosophies for packet delivery.

### Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)

TCP guarantees that every single byte sent will arrive in order, without duplicates, or the connection will throw an error:

- 3-Way Handshake (`SYN` -> `SYN-ACK` -> `ACK`)
- Sequence and Acknowledgment numbers
- Congestion control and sliding windows
- Head-of-line blocking if packet loss occurs

### User Datagram Protocol (UDP)

UDP sends packets with minimal overhead and zero delivery guarantees:

```text
+-----------------------+
| Source Port (16 bits) |
| Dest Port   (16 bits) |
| Length      (16 bits) |
| Checksum    (16 bits) |
+-----------------------+
| Data Payload          |
+-----------------------+
```

> When latency matters more than a single lost frame—such as real-time audio/video streaming, multiplayer gaming, or QUIC (HTTP/3)—UDP is the protocol of choice.
